mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 2.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS never exceeds 2.5% in the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 consecutive such labor-market tightening months, the 5-day forward returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects strengthening economic momentum and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥3% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform a risk-free rate proxy by at least 1% (t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for two consecutive months suggests the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, reducing discount rate expectations and supporting higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 100 such deflationary months, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a neutral market (zero-move) portfolio (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly real personal income (GDPC1) grows faster than CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% for three consecutive months, it indicates a real wage gain, which tends to produce a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not positive in more than 70% of windows (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% followed by a decline in labor force participation (HOUST) suggests a tightening labor market, which can precede equity risk-on flows and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND HOUST falls by ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: In 50 such episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in retail sales (PAYEMS) below trend, when accompanied by a sustained rise in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence catalog), would typically signal softening demand; however, in the absence of confidence data, this sketch is reserved for future extension. candidate_trigger: PAYEMS below trend for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20 such weak-demand months, the 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 40% of cases (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side inflation pressure measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains persistently above 3.0% for four consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter monetary policy and higher real rates.
failure_condition: Across 30 such inflationary episodes, the 20-day forward returns do not underperform a risk-free rate proxy (t-test, p > 0.10).
